mapper.select:
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 1: CALCULATE POSTED ACCOUNT ACTIVITY -- ======================================================
/* Aggregate all POSTED ledger entries through the selected reporting cutoff date.
We first use a universal debit-positive accounting amount:
debits - credits
This amount is later converted to the correct normal-balance direction based on account_type.
COUNT(*) records how many posted ledger entries contribute to each account.
This allows the Java service to detect unclassified accounts with posted activity, even when their final balance is zero. */
WITH posted_totals AS (
SELECT
-- ============================================== -- BUSINESS AND ACCOUNT IDENTIFICATION -- ==============================================
le.business_id,
le.account_id,
-- ============================================== -- DEBIT-POSITIVE NET ACCOUNT ACTIVITY -- ==============================================
/* PostgreSQL NUMERIC arithmetic maintains exact decimal precision.
Examples:
Debit 500.00, Credit 0.00 Result: 500.00
Debit 0.00, Credit 500.00 Result: -500.00
We preserve the sign here. */
SUM( le.debit - le.credit ) AS net_debit_balance,
-- ============================================== -- NUMBER OF POSTED LEDGER ENTRIES -- ==============================================
COUNT(*) AS posted_entry_count
-- ================================================== -- LEDGER ENTRIES -- ==================================================
FROM ledger_entries le
-- ================================================== -- MATCH ENTRIES TO THEIR TRANSACTION HEADERS -- ==================================================
/* Both business_id and transaction_id participate in the join.
This prevents data from another business entering the report. */
INNER JOIN transactions t ON t.business_id = le.business_id AND t.id = le.transaction_id
-- ================================================== -- FILTER ACCOUNTING ACTIVITY -- ==================================================
WHERE le.business_id = #{businessId}
-- ================================================ -- INCLUDE ONLY FINALIZED TRANSACTIONS -- ================================================
/* DRAFT transactions do not affect the Balance Sheet.
Only POSTED journal entries count. */
AND t.status = 'POSTED'
-- ================================================ -- APPLY INCLUSIVE REPORTING DATE -- ================================================
/* The Balance Sheet reports cumulative balances as of one date.
Unlike the Income Statement, there is no reporting start date. */
AND t.transaction_date <= #{asOfDate}
-- ================================================== -- GROUP POSTED ACTIVITY BY ACCOUNT -- ==================================================
GROUP BY le.business_id, le.account_id )
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 2: SELECT GENERAL LEDGER ACCOUNTS -- ======================================================
SELECT
-- ============================================== -- ACCOUNT IDENTIFICATION -- ==============================================
a.id AS account_id,
a.code,
a.name,
-- ============================================== -- ACCOUNT CLASSIFICATION -- ==============================================
a.account_type,
a.reporting_group,
-- ============================================== -- ACCOUNT STATUS -- ==============================================
a.is_active,
-- ================================================== -- STEP 3: CALCULATE NORMAL ACCOUNT BALANCES -- ==================================================
/* Different account types have different normal balance directions.
ASSET: Debits - Credits
EXPENSE: Debits - Credits
LIABILITY: Credits - Debits
EQUITY: Credits - Debits
REVENUE: Credits - Debits
posted_totals stores:
Debits - Credits
Therefore:
ASSET and EXPENSE: Use the stored amount directly.
LIABILITY, EQUITY, and REVENUE: Negate the stored amount.
Negative balances are preserved.
We do not use ABS() or GREATEST() because that would hide legitimate negative account balances. */
CASE
-- ========================================== -- ASSETS — DEBIT NORMAL -- ==========================================
WHEN a.account_type = 'ASSET' THEN
COALESCE( pt.net_debit_balance, 0::NUMERIC )
-- ========================================== -- EXPENSES — DEBIT NORMAL -- ==========================================
WHEN a.account_type = 'EXPENSE' THEN
COALESCE( pt.net_debit_balance, 0::NUMERIC )
-- ========================================== -- LIABILITIES — CREDIT NORMAL -- ==========================================
WHEN a.account_type = 'LIABILITY' THEN
-COALESCE( pt.net_debit_balance, 0::NUMERIC )
-- ========================================== -- EQUITY — CREDIT NORMAL -- ==========================================
WHEN a.account_type = 'EQUITY' THEN
-COALESCE( pt.net_debit_balance, 0::NUMERIC )
-- ========================================== -- REVENUE — CREDIT NORMAL -- ==========================================
WHEN a.account_type = 'REVENUE' THEN
-COALESCE( pt.net_debit_balance, 0::NUMERIC )
-- ========================================== -- DEFENSIVE DEFAULT -- ==========================================
ELSE 0::NUMERIC
END AS balance,
-- ================================================== -- STEP 4: RETURN POSTED ENTRY COUNT -- ==================================================
/* Include accounts with no posted history.
Such accounts have:
balance = 0 postedEntryCount = 0
Accounts with offsetting entries may have a zero balance but a positive posted entry count. */
COALESCE( pt.posted_entry_count, 0::BIGINT ) AS posted_entry_count
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 5: INCLUDE ALL ELIGIBLE BUSINESS ACCOUNTS -- ======================================================
FROM accounts a
-- ====================================================== -- JOIN CALCULATED POSTED BALANCES -- ======================================================
/* LEFT JOIN ensures accounts without posted transactions are still returned.
We do not filter by is_active because inactive accounts may contain historical accounting balances.
We do not filter by reporting_group because unclassified accounts must remain visible for financial statement validation. */
LEFT JOIN posted_totals pt ON pt.business_id = a.business_id AND pt.account_id = a.id
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 6: RESTRICT ACCOUNTS TO ONE BUSINESS -- ======================================================
WHERE a.business_id = #{businessId}
-- ================================================ -- EXCLUDE NON-POSTABLE GROUPING ACCOUNTS -- ================================================
/* V7 introduced account hierarchies.
Non-postable parent accounts organize the Chart of Accounts.
These accounts cannot receive direct journal entries.
Their child accounts already appear individually in this query.
Including parent subtotals as separate financial balances would double-count financial activity.
We therefore return only posting accounts. */
AND a.is_postable = TRUE
-- ================================================ -- INCLUDE ALL FIVE FUNDAMENTAL ACCOUNT TYPES -- ================================================
/* ASSET, LIABILITY, and EQUITY accounts contribute directly to the Balance Sheet.
REVENUE and EXPENSE accounts contribute indirectly through unclosed earnings.
All five account types must be available to the Java service. */
AND a.account_type IN ( 'ASSET', 'LIABILITY', 'EQUITY', 'REVENUE', 'EXPENSE' )
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 7: SORT ACCOUNT BALANCES -- ======================================================
/* Return financial accounts in a stable order.
1. Assets 2. Liabilities 3. Equity 4. Revenue 5. Expenses
Within each account type, sort by user-defined account code and account ID.
The BalanceSheetService will organize the first three types into their V7 reporting groups.
Revenue and Expense will be aggregated into unclosed earnings. */
ORDER BY
CASE
WHEN a.account_type = 'ASSET' THEN 1
WHEN a.account_type = 'LIABILITY' THEN 2
WHEN a.account_type = 'EQUITY' THEN 3
WHEN a.account_type = 'REVENUE' THEN 4
WHEN a.account_type = 'EXPENSE' THEN 5
ELSE 6
END,
a.code,
a.id
